effect_size.excerpt: Despite a large range in intake, no association was observed between fruit, vegetables or antioxidant nutrients and RCC risk. sample_size.excerpt: In the current analysis, we included all participants in the clinical trials and the observational study except for women who enrolled in the Dietary Modification clinical trial (n = 48,835) who had a history of any cancer other than nonmelanoma skin cancers at study entry 7 , 10 , 12 or who had implausible energy intakes (<600 or >5000 kcal daily) at baseline (n = 4067). headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 5 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.76 (95% CI: 0.62–0.94), suggesting that Vitamin C is associated with a lower risk of renal cell carcinoma. These findings were supported by moderate between-study heterogeneity (I² = 38.56%), suggesting some variability in the results across studies.
